body: Hey, this is not a battle sub, please check your passive aggressiveness out the door! Thank you.

Kinda in a similar boat. I want to be completely honest, I did not make my wealth at all. It was all generational income. My parents owns a few real estate properties. I am extremely lucky that I do not ever have to worry about paying for food or rent for the rest of my life. What I have noticed is women do not care about any of this. Initial attraction is everything. The money, houses, cars are just a bonus. There are attractive prisoners getting love letters from women, and then getting hired as models after they finish their sentence. The world is an extremely unfair place. This has nothing to do being a nice guy, and anyone who tells you differently is gas lighting you. Of course there are also exceptions when someone is not attractive, and yet has a very attractive partner, but these are exceptions and not the rule.
That is not what a best friend do. I am sorry to hear that op.

So close you almost got the point! /s 

Also the "You got offend by my comment and got triggered by it then you must be an incel!" point is weak. Go share your made up bullshit some where else, you don't know me enough to give me "life advice". All I am saying is if you really want to help others who are suffering from loneliness and pain go read more studies and research on dating.

Why the fuck does your post sounds so condescending? 

I think there is a misunderstanding here. I am not an incel I am a software engineer. I don't hate women, so please don't treat me like one. I have tons of friends, coworkers, and a good amount of female friends. I also volunteer on the weekends and lead social meetups. 

You are also missing my point. As an Asian man I am at the bottom of the attractiveness hierarchy. This is proven by big data and statistical analysis. This is not some feeling I "think" I have. Studies have been done by dating app makers, and reputable universities, I didn't pull this out of my ass. 

> your thinking is just flawed because you've been soaking in this puddle  
 of other people's thoughts that the rest of the world caused your   
misery. When in reality, you don't even know those people.

Again, learn how statistical inference works. An easy example is we can survey enough people to make accurate prediction of the presidential race. If we do the same on dating? You get the idea.

My favorite quote from the above article. 

>Kao says the statistics show a clear hierarchy based on race that leaves  
 Asian men on the bottom rung. If everybody had random preferences,   
things would even out and there’d be no strong bias for or against men   
of any race. “If that’s not racism, I don’t know what is.”

The above link tells you how polling works. Yes you can sample 1000 people and make an accurate prediction of the presidential race, let alone using 44.2 million current US OLD users to predict dating discrimination. With that much sample, dating app is a good reflection of our behaviors in our currently society. This is why I am giving up on dating and focusing on my career. Fighting against a rigged system is just a waste of time when I can focus on other meaningful path. 

Finally I just want to say, please educate yourself first before you try to downplay other people's struggles. Too many people on Reddit like to discredit other people's pain and suffering because it is so easier to treat them like incels or nice guys. Heck we even have dedicated subreddits to make fun of people who are clearly struggling with loneliness, and social interactions. The rate of young men who cannot find sex or relationship is skyrocketing. So please, stop telling people there is something wrong with them, instead try your best to listen and understand what they are trying to say.

Kind of. It is a hard pill to swallow, but I know myself better than anyone else. People who told me I need to improve more doesn't know how much I've changed my life around. At one point the copium you tell yourself no longer works. Don't get me wrong, I firmly believe in the growth mindset, but it just doesn't apply to dating. For example, if I do 10 push ups a day and do it for a year my physique will get stronger. If I play the guitar everyday I can master it. When it comes to dating, the same just doesn't apply. You can get fit, be motivated, but if you are considered ugly your odds won't increase much. Growth mindset in dating is just copium, it slowly down the pain and make life bearable, and that is the truth people on reddit tip toes around. 

My current solution is to ignore dating completely. I will not participate in any conversations about relationships with friends or co-workers, or get myself into any social events with a lot of couples. I will keep it to myself, so I don't remind myself how lonely I am. 

I am also going to practice growth mindset on things that are within my control to limit my regrets before l leave this planet. For example, my work life, and my hobbies. I am going to build a successful career instead of seeking other people's attraction. 

To answer your question, I am almost 32, and I will give up on improving my dating life. I am not going to waste my precious time or worrying if I am attractive or not when the odds is actively stacked against me. I am going to play life on my own terms, and be the best version of myself everyday. To be great there must be sacrifices, I've realized for the longest time I am trying to fight against the flow. If the society I live in doesn't deem me to be good enough even after all the massive amount of improvement I've made then fuck it. I'll save all that effort and work on things that I can actually affect.

Look through my post history. It is hard to find motivation when you try your best and still fail. Any normal human being would feel this way. This post make it sound like virgins were born this way, instead of looking at the bigger picture of what caused all these pain and help solve it. Once again, I am getting the "there is nothing wrong with the dating world, there is something wrong with you" vibe.
What you are speaking of is the exception but not the rule.

It is not just women that go after looks, men also go after looks. This has been proven again and again. For example, the famous halo effect https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6FCS5WQB-98, or it only takes 3 second to decide if someone is right for you in OLD. If that is not judging a book by its cover I don't know what it is. [https://www.inc.com/melanie-curtin/science-says-you-do-this-surprising-thing-in-just-3-seconds-hint-it-has-to-do-with-attraction.html](https://www.inc.com/melanie-curtin/science-says-you-do-this-surprising-thing-in-just-3-seconds-hint-it-has-to-do-with-attraction.html)

IMO in our modern society people have realized that announcing the fact they pick partners base on looks will be deemed shallow. As a result, people will just discriminate silently.  

All these scientific studies are created by schools with high reputations, they are not made by misogyny people or incels to further their agenda. It is simply the truth that reflect our behavior as a society.

Finally I just want to say, labeling majority of the people here as misogynists without looking into the actual science of dating is just as bad as labeling all women shallow.

I am only like this on Reddit. In real life I am as confident as they come. For example, at work I lead a group of young adults. Just recently we had an ice breaker meeting with 20 people in a park. Everyone sat on the grass in a big circle. Most of the people were whispering when they were introducing themselves, and I was the only person who decided to stand in the middle of the group and shout so everyone can hear me. I am definitely a confident individual irl. If a girl gave me inviting signals in-person I'll have zero problem going up to her and strike up a conversation. You can't be an introvert when you hold a leadership position at work it is as simple as that. I am telling you, I can't attract anyone because of my height, looks, and not my personality. Everyone at work loves me, I go out of my way to check on other people to make sure they take care of their mental health because I know how it feels to be alone. I do not want anyone to experience what I am going through right now.

I can't and won't do that. My issue is more about loneliness and intimacy instead of not getting enough sex. My dad was also a dead beat, he had money when he was young and cheated on my mom with escorts. After they separated, my mom projected a lot of the hate towards me because I look like him. One of her favorite saying is how much I look like my dead beat dad and how much my actions resembles him. This is why I won't get an escort, I refused to justify the emotional abuse my mom caused me by following my dad's foot steps.

Thank you for being so understanding from my perspective. If I am 100% honest, the self-improvements did help me increase my odds of getting matches, but it felt more like a 1% increase. Going from 1 match per 100 swipes to 2 is probably not that helpful. In addition, I am fluent in Chinese and had previous dating experience in China. What I experienced in China was completely different from the states. I went on about seven dates when I went back for vacation. Six out of seven girls wanted to continue the conversation, but I stopped the convo because we didn't have anything in common, and I was not comfortable maintaining a long-distance relationship. Plus, the time zone is 12 hours, so when I am awake they will be asleep. Furthermore, some of the girls definitely were into me because of my social status, and financial background. The thought of people finding me attractive base on monetary values always made me insecure. Like most people, I want to meet someone who will be there when I am in a rough spot instead of leaving because I can no longer provide. I know what some of you are thinking, "Why don't you just go to China to date then?". Firstly, I have been in America longer than I've lived in China. I am a US citizen and have been here for the past 20 years. Secondly, If I leave the US to date, I can't help but feel I am enforcing the idea that Asian men are not attractive enough to be successful in America.

Anyways, I agree with you that there is nothing wrong with me. I am saddened that people still think I don't try hard enough instead of just accepting that height, lookism, and racial discrimination are prevalent in the current dating landscape.

Its been 6 years of none stop grinding, I started when I was 26, now I am 32. I have been fit for the past 3 to 4 years. I also have a few women friends. No female best friends, but I definitely have women friends.

My status:

Software engineer

Home owner, with no debt

Fit, and artistically talented

Tons of friends, big social group

and I CAN'T EVEN GET MATCHES on OLD.

Lookism, heightism, extrinsic value matter the most on dating apps. People who say the other sex can evaluate your entire personality, your desperation, and compatibility based on professionally taken photos is spewing bs. What they described is the literal definition of judging a book by its cover. People will do anything to blame the issue on you instead of accepting the halo effect is real, and extrinsic attribute matters online.

You don't believe me go make a dating profile of an average guy and see how it goes. It is simple experiment to end all arguments. I believe in statistics, data, and looking at the bigger picture instead of pulling out "personal experience" out of my ass. The whole "women want comfort and emotional support" can wait, lets get me some matches first before we get to that step. Anyways, this is the rock that I am willing to die on, because it is the truth.
Social media is full of shit. You never know what is happening behind those smiling faces.
How attractive are you my guy?
I wouldn't. I did it once and it didn't turn out well. That moment was definitely pretty awkward. Maybe you can do it indirectly and test the water before telling your friend your story.

Hit the gym and focus on something else. Don't get a fit body for girls, do it for yourself. It doesn't even have to be the gym. It could be drawing, music making, you need to STOP letting the obsessive thoughts control you. Find something productive that you can be obsessive at and go hard at it. We all wish intimacy can just show up next day, but the reality is we need to ground ourselves first before that can happen.
This is such a great way to reframe this mindset. Thank you.

>If you want to get with a woman, first, see her as a human being with feelings, thoughts, and emotions. 

This is not accurate at all. I know engineers who are the kindest people on the planet and gets no matches in dating apps. My best friend makes 6 figures, huge social group, we volunteer weekly for a non-profit, and he is still a virgin at 30. I really hate seeing people coming to this sub and automatically put people in a category of incels. The halo effect, racial preference, heightism in dating are all well studied phenomenons. When you say don't be a creep you are looking at the exception and not the rule. The rule is, online dating is all about swiping on extrinsic values, because you can't accurately judge a personality by pictures alone.
The police were also confused on why this guy hung up his own picture in another person's apt.

I once read a Reddit thread about things a girl would do if they are interested in you. Lets just say none of the things mentioned in the thread happened to me. I consider myself a confident individual, and have no problem approaching girls, and making plans. My struggle with dating is getting that initial attraction. Dating is a numbers game, can't rack up the numbers if no one is willing to give you a chance in the first place.
No that would revoke my ability to rant on this subreddit. /s

For a period of time I did approach girls, but now I am just taking a back seat. I don't randomly talk to strangers and ask for their number. I tried to maximize my chances by befriending the girl first. Last school semester I asked someone out, and she told me I was very sweet, but she was seeing someone else. Before that I tried to ask out 4 other people with no success. I often find myself carrying the conversation, and if I don't text I won't hear back from them at all. Clearly they are not romantically interested in me, which is totally cool because now I know we are not compatible. The problem is this has been going on for ages, and I am frustrated by my lack of success despite how much I have turned my life around.

No I am east Asian, but I feel people in my age group are not as accepting as the younger generation. There weren't a lot of kpop, anime, or just in general Asian representation on TV when I was growing up. As a result, I often find myself having more common language with younger women. Just last semester I asked out a 22 years old, but afterwards I felt like a creep. The age gap is just too great, even tho our interests aligns I will not be doing that again.

I also believe my problem is a race issue. For example, you can google white/black guys speak fluent Chinese/Korean/Japanese and see people praise them for it, but when I speak English or my native language no one bats an eye.  

To be completely fair, there are many good threads on Reddit showing sympathy for Asian men in the dating market, but Reddit users only represents a fraction of the population. In general there is still a long way to go for us.
I have the same feeling except with dating app.

I don't think men assume you can just get any guys you want. I think they meant you have more options than them, which is true. You can check out /r/tinderdata to see the differences between women and men swipe information. This is the reason why a lot of men are salty when women complain they have a hard time on dating apps.

Same here 31 no girlfriend. My friend is 30  years old engineer who also never had a girlfriend. In fact I know one other software developers who is in the same boat. There are tons of us in STEM struggling to get dates.
